request.prompt: Create a production 3D-game MATERIAL ATLAS, a perfectly square image divided into an exact 2 by 2 grid of four equal square swatches, edge to edge, no gutters, no borders, no text. This is flat albedo paint for an original painterly Cold War underground silo environment in Nautilus Engine, matching hand-painted gouache game assets with confident broad brushwork and restrained fine detail. Each quadrant is a near-seamless orthographic material swatch, viewed straight on with uniform neutral illumination, no perspective, no objects or architectural scene, no baked directional shadows, no cast highlights, no symbols, no rivets or pipes, no stairs, no markings. TOP LEFT: warm grey poured concrete, broad mottled mineral tones and subtle trowelled/formwork memory, soft wear, no brick or block grid, no deep cracks. TOP RIGHT: faded industrial seafoam green enamel on steel, broad brush variation, restrained scuffs and small worn paint patches, mostly intact flat colour. BOTTOM LEFT: warm ivory painted institutional wall/enamel, matte cream, gentle brush texture and subdued age stains, no tiles, no grid. BOTTOM RIGHT: dark charcoal blue-grey steel, broad quiet directional rubbed strokes, subtle warm brown oxidation, no grating or checker pattern. Keep the four swatches at comparable visual scale. Colours should remain readable at a distant isometric camera. Polished painterly texture artwork, NOT photorealistic, NOT a mood board, exact square four-quadrant layout.

transforms: Selected output copied byte-for-byte; no raster editing.
